records.mutation: kill the wrong source of uncertainty: ignorance comes from the unknown reading, not from many factorizations, so intersect feasibility tests across readings
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent hint scored 0/8 and 5 of 8 hit the token cap; every rollout attributed "I don't know" to the display having many factor pairs, then correctly noticed that a speaker's own value pins the partner uniquely, declared a contradiction, and either looped enumerating pairs until truncation or picked an arbitrary factor. The incumbent flags label ambiguity but still frames uncertainty as multiple partners, so I replaced that with the correct rule -- uncertainty comes only from the unknown reading -- and turned it into an intersect-the-feasibility-tests procedure that terminates quickly.

records.mutation: replace the problem-specific Mobius substitution with the general modulus route (|z-a|=k|z-b| squared into a circle), warning off the angle-parametrization path
records.subagent_summary: All eight fresh rollouts were correct this round and none truncated, so train is saturated at 1.0 while heldout stays at 0.125; the incumbent's remaining value is mostly its literal naming of this problem's substitution, which cannot transfer. The shortest, cleanest rollouts avoided angle parametrization and instead took absolute values to get a fixed-ratio distance condition, squared it with the conjugate identity, and completed the square, while the only prior failure came from sign slips inside the Moebius-parametrization branch; I therefore promoted the modulus route as the transferable technique and kept exactness, one spot-check, and early commitment.

records.mutation: keep the sector/symmetry core but compress it and add budget discipline: stop re-litigating once the value repeats
records.subagent_summary: Four of eight rollouts were correct, and the failure mode has shifted: all eight reached the correct value early in reasoning (within the first ~7k characters), but every one of the four failures then kept re-testing rotation angles and re-deriving the setup until it hit the 16384-token cap with the reasoning block still open, so nothing was scored. The containment warning from the incumbent is now working, so this revision shortens that clause and spends the freed tokens on explicit budget discipline: one clean overlap argument plus one extreme case, record the exact value immediately, and treat a repeated value as a stop signal rather than grounds for another angle sweep.

records.mutation: separate the degree-d root cap from the d+1 interpolation count, assert the summed budget is already in the asked-for units, and compress the impossibility-branch exit
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored 0 and none reached the intended count: four hit the token limit while relooping on a self-inflicted impossibility (forcing one polynomial's own consecutive difference to be constant), and the finishers answered either the number of available objects or a bare degree/interpolation count. One rollout derived the correct product of per-object budgets but then rejected it as "not directly applicable" and reinterpreted it as a single object's cap, so the revision distinguishes the root cap from the interpolation count, states that the summed budget is already the quantity being asked for, and shortens the exit from impossibility branches to reduce truncation.

records.mutation: compress to a terse generic name-reduce-discard-crosscheck rule, roughly half the length of prior rewrites
records.subagent_summary: All eight fresh rollouts were correct at about 9.4k completion tokens, so train accuracy is saturated and only transfer can move J. The real crux in every successful rollout was rejecting the degenerate root of the reduced one-variable equation and then cross-checking the area by a second formula, so I kept exactly those two transferable moves. Both prior rewrites were long generic discipline lists (136-150 tokens) and lost heldout against a 73-token incumbent, so this proposal tests brevity: about 68 tokens of dense imperatives with no setup-specific vocabulary.

records.mutation: add forced-outcome (0 or 1) trap plus total-moves = items x legs and LIFO first-arrival-is-bottom mechanics
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent scored 0/8 (one rollout hit the 16384-token cap while dithering; the other seven terminated normally), so length is only a marginal issue. Two rollouts newly collapsed the process to a deterministic outcome and reported certainty or impossibility, several miscounted the total number of moves by charging one move per item instead of one per item per leg, and most still fell back on an asserted uniform-permutation shortcut for the second part. The revision keeps the symmetry warning that transferred well, forbids an unargued 0-or-1 claim without two exhibited reachable end states, states the moves = items x legs count and the last-in-first-out fact that a destination's bottom is its earliest arrival, and pushes for an early committed result.

records.mutation: pin the n-family scaling rule up front and forbid renegotiating the setup mid-solution
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling scored 2 of 8; both successes came from plain elimination on n = 2, 3, 4 followed by an immediate commit to the factored pattern, while all 6 failures hit the 16384-token cap. The dominant failure was not arithmetic but repeated renegotiation of the small-case setup: rollouts kept re-deriving how many conditions the reduced instance should have, then adopted a polynomial reinterpretation that contradicted their own hand-solved case and restarted instead of trusting it. The revision therefore makes the n-family scaling rule an explicit one-time step, forbids revisiting it, and instructs the student to discard a contradicting reinterpretation rather than the verified arithmetic.

records.mutation: keep incumbent text verbatim, name gcd explicitly, and append a short domain-neutral transfer clause (fix per-unit-vs-total scope once, gcd = largest admissible count, commit then back-verify)
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored reward 1 with clean stops at 2.7-5.6k tokens, so train_i is saturated at 1.0 and every remaining point of gain must come from transfer. Rounds 1 and 2 both rewrote the hint wholesale and each collapsed train (0.25 and 0.5) while transfer barely moved, so this round preserves the incumbent sentences verbatim and only appends reusable strategy. The rollouts show two concrete, repeatable stalls: 20-80 oscillations per rollout over whether a listed figure is per-unit or a collection total, and 6-24 restatements of the maximum-feasible-count clause before concluding the gcd, so I name the gcd inline and add a decide-once/commit-then-back-verify rule.

records.mutation: name the recenter-plus-antisymmetric-ansatz construction concretely, add add/subtract-the-two-given-values solve step, structural (non-expanding) verification, and an ugly-fractions abort signal with a one-switch cap
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts split 4/8 correct with a sharp pattern: every success terminated under 10k tokens after committing to a shared-center antisymmetric ansatz and solving the two given values by adding/subtracting them, while all four failures ran to the 16384-token cap - two after reverting to full coefficient expansion of the composition, one lost in divisor-hunting over ugly fractions, and one that reached the right ansatz but then tried to verify it by brute expansion. The revision therefore spells out the recentering construction and its two-equation solve, replaces expansion-based verification with a symmetry check, and gives an explicit abort signal plus a one-switch cap so the student stops re-deriving instead of burning the budget.

records.mutation: attack the premature-shortcut failure mode: force falsification of any guessed closed form against a literal small-case trace, forbid assuming period 2 from swap-shaped stages, and require exact counts at two sizes
records.subagent_summary: Only 2 of 8 rollouts were correct. The dominant new failure was premature abstraction into a plausible-sounding shortcut: three finishing rollouts all asserted the process was a fixed block shift or a product of disjoint 2-cycles and therefore had period 2, without ever tracing labels far enough to falsify that claim, and the four token-capped rollouts burned the budget on symbolic index formulas after abandoning small cases. The revision therefore keeps the incumbent's concrete-trace instinct but reorients it as a falsification test on any guessed shortcut, names the swap-implies-period-2 trap explicitly, and requires exact counts at two sizes before generalizing.
